svg.text: 🧱 Component Map — Imports, Classes & Methods (for new Python users)
Central settings — reads .env file, validates all credentials and RAG parameters
NEBIUS_API_KEY · NEO4J_URI · NEO4J_PASSWORD · CHROMA_PATH · RAG_CHUNK_SIZE · RAG_TOP_K
— @lru_cache singleton: call once, reuse everywhere. Reads .env automatically via pydantic_settings.
Fetches FDA food enforcement data — REST API and pre-downloaded bulk JSON
— calls openFDA REST API with retry
— maps raw FDA fields to standard dict shape
Fetches USDA FSIS recalls via undocumented JSON API (RSS is 404) — 1,759 Class I+II records
— GET /fsis/api/recall/v/1, returns 1,759 Class I+II records (2,006 all classes)
— maps API fields to standard dict; sets _is_fda_structured=True for fast path
Note: RSS feed returns 404. This JSON endpoint is used by the USDA website itself — undocumented but stable.
Pulls CDC foodborne outbreak data — fail-fast on 404 (Socrata endpoint currently offline)
— Socrata JSON API · no retry · returns [] immediately on 404
— maps CDC fields to standard dict
⚠ Offline: Socrata endpoint returns 404. Fail-fast — no retry wasted on a hard 404.
Two deliberate semantic chunks per recall — no arbitrary splitting, every chunk self-contained and retrievable
chunk_type "summary": product · manufacturer · hazard · reason (WHAT — for semantic search)
chunk_type "detail": states · lot numbers · dates · distribution (WHERE/WHEN — no overlap needed)
Extracts product name, hazard, states, UPC codes from recall text — fast path skips LLM entirely
product_name · manufacturer · hazard_type · lot_numbers · upc_codes · severity
— direct field mapping, 0 LLM calls, used for all 27k FDA records
— builds product image URL from UPC barcode (EAN-13 split into 3-digit groups)
Stores and searches 58k recall text chunks using semantic embeddings (meaning-based search)
wraps ChromaDB — a local vector database that stores text + its embedding
— writes batches of 5,000 (ChromaDB max per call is 5,461)
— enriches query with household context before searching
Neo4j knowledge graph — stores supply-chain relationships between recalls, manufacturers, regions, users
class GraphStore: (context manager — use with "with GraphStore() as gs:")
— MERGE: writes without duplicates. Builds Manufacturer→Recall→Region links.
— traverses graph to find ALL recalls from one manufacturer (supply-chain blindspot fix)
— follows User→Region←Recall path with keyword + severity filters
Household profiles — stores dietary habits, location, and family context used for personalised matching
user_id · name · email · states · household_profile · has_children
— reads user_profiles.json, returns list[UserProfile]. Called by both pipelines.
Delivers AI-written alerts via console, JSON log — and future email/SMS/WhatsApp
channel router — currently console + JSON, stubs for email/SMS ready
— routes to console print + appends to alerts_log.json
LangGraph stateful pipeline — orchestrates fetch → extract → chunk → store as a state machine
raw_recalls · processed_recalls · chunks · indexed_count · errors · skip_vectors · skip_neo4j
TypedDict: typed dict — LangGraph reads/writes state through it at each step
Matches recalls to user profiles using dual RAG, evaluates risk with LLM, fires alerts
— 7-day eval_cache.json · skips LLM on hit · 8 workers · 45s timeout each
Cache key: (user_id, recall_id) · first scan calls LLM · repeat scans complete in seconds
— disables Qwen3 thinking mode to prevent empty responses
LangGraph fan-out — parallel VectorRAG + GraphRAG, then LLM synthesises one answer
query · user_id · vector_results · graph_results · final_answer · history
— 3 LLM calls: vector answer, graph answer, merge
Fan-out: START connects to 2 nodes simultaneously — LangGraph runs them in parallel
errors: Annotated[list, operator.add] — allows both parallel nodes to write errors
Streamlit web app — 6 tabs, auto-scan on startup, sidebar profile/model selector, custom CSS severity badges
Auto-scan: checks if alerts_log.json is older than 24 h on every page load → fires matching pipeline in background thread (daemon=True)
st.session_state: Streamlit's way to persist variables between user interactions within one browser session
